paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy performance of various probing setups on multilingual BERT models under different perturbation conditions, as described in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis represents Accuracy, ranging from 70 to 95 in increments of 5, while the horizontal axis lists 13 distinct experimental conditions grouped by model configuration and perturbation type. The first two bars (blue) represent probes applied to the embedding layer and the first layer of the pre-trained model, achieving accuracies of approximately 80% and 82%, respectively. The next five bars (green) correspond to models with a pre-trained embedding layer but randomly initialized upper layers, under five perturbation variants (no perturbation, +B₂, +L₂, +R₂, +permute), with accuracy values hovering around 80–82%. The following five bars (red) reflect models where both the embedding layer and upper layers are randomly initialized, under the same perturbation variants, yielding lower accuracies between 71% and 74%. The final two bars (orange) represent the unperturbed, fully trained models, with the lighter orange bar at ~90% and the darker orange bar reaching ~92%, indicating the highest performance. The chart visually contrasts the impact of randomization and perturbation on probing accuracy, with the unperturbed trained models significantly outperforming all randomized variants.
